• Collaboration seeks to strengthen domestic supply chains for critical metals and unlock value from under-utilised plant reverts
Impact: Positive (Adds critical-metal recovery capability and circular-economy linkage, but the MoU is a non-binding framework with no stated value or timeline)

DIGILOGIC SYSTEMS Q2 CONCALL: H1 REVENUE UP 91% YOY, EBITDA UP 126% & MANAGEMENT MAINTAINS 25–30% FY27 REVENUE GROWTH GUIDANCE

• MANAGEMENT MAINTAINS FY27 REVENUE GROWTH GUIDANCE OF 25–30%, IMPLYING APPROXIMATELY ₹97.5–101.4 CR REVENUE AGAINST ₹78 CR IN FY26

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS FY27 EBITDA & NET PROFIT GROWTH OF APPROXIMATELY 30–35%, SUPPORTED BY DEFENCE PROJECT EXECUTION

• H1 REVENUE UP 91% YOY TO ₹34.96 CR, WHILE EBITDA SURGED 126% TO ₹7.81 CR

• H1 NET PROFIT JUMPED 151% YOY TO ₹4.76 CR, COMPARED WITH ₹1.90 CR LAST YEAR

• H1 EBITDA MARGIN IMPROVED TO APPROXIMATELY 22.3% FROM 18.9% YOY, SUPPORTED BY HIGHER REVENUE & OPERATING LEVERAGE

• COMPANY EXECUTED 36 PROJECTS WORTH APPROXIMATELY ₹33.18 CR DURING H1, SUPPORTED BY DEFENCE & DRDO CUSTOMER DEMAND

• CONFIRMED ORDER BOOK STANDS AT APPROXIMATELY ₹20 CR, WITH AN ADDITIONAL ₹54 CR TENDER PIPELINE AT VARIOUS STAGES OF EVALUATION & NEGOTIATION

• MANAGEMENT TARGETS CONVERSION & BILLING OF THE ₹54 CR TENDER PIPELINE AROUND FEBRUARY 2027, WITH APPROXIMATELY 60% RELATED TO REPEAT ORDERS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS CORE TEST & MEASUREMENT SYSTEMS BUSINESS TO SUSTAIN APPROXIMATELY 25–30% GROWTH, DRIVEN BY DEFENCE ELECTRONICS DEMAND

• COMPANY PARTICIPATES IN AT LEAST 10 DEFENCE PROGRAMS, INCLUDING MRSAM & ANTI-DRONE SYSTEMS, WITH APPROXIMATELY 3–4 PROGRAMS ALREADY IN PRODUCTION

• PROJECT UDAAN CONSTRUCTION IS UNDERWAY, WITH CIVIL WORK TARGETED FOR COMPLETION AROUND MARCH 2027, FOLLOWED BY EQUIPMENT INSTALLATION & CERTIFICATION

• PROJECT UDAAN WILL EXPAND THE COMPANY INTO ELECTRONICS MANUFACTURING & SYSTEM DESIGN, WITH BUILD-TO-PRINT SERVICES EXPECTED TO COMMERCIALIZE FIRST

• ABHEDHYA SYSTEMS TARGETS COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION DURING H2 FY29, WHILE NEW GIMBAL & SINGLE-BOARD COMPUTER PRODUCTS OFFER INITIAL ANNUAL REVENUE POTENTIAL OF ₹3–4 CR

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS CURRENT PROFITABILITY LEVELS TO REMAIN SUSTAINABLE, WHILE ELEVATED INVENTORY IS EXPECTED TO BE LARGELY CONSUMED BY MARCH 2027

• MANAGEMENT REMAINS POSITIVE ON DEFENCE ELECTRONICS OPPORTUNITIES, BUT ₹54 CR TENDER CONVERSION, H2 REVENUE EXECUTION, PROJECT UDAAN CERTIFICATION & WORKING-CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS REMAIN KEY RISKS

INDO RAMA SYNTHETICS Q2 CONCALL : NET PROFIT UP 202% YOY, MANAGEMENT EXPECTS FY27 EBITDA ABOVE ₹400 CR & ANNOUNCES ₹200 CR SPECIALTY EXPANSION

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS FY27 REVENUE TO EXCEED ₹5,000 CR, WITH EBITDA TARGETED ABOVE ₹400 CR

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS EBITDA MARGINS OF APPROXIMATELY 9.9% TO REMAIN SUSTAINABLE OVER THE NEXT TWO QUARTERS, WITH A LONGER-TERM AMBITION TO ACHIEVE DOUBLE-DIGIT MARGINS

• MANAGEMENT EXPECTS FY27 SALES VOLUMES OF APPROXIMATELY 4 LAKH TONNES, BELOW FY26'S 4.75 LAKH TONNES, WITH RECOVERY ABOVE FY26 LEVELS TARGETED IN FY28

• Q2 NET PROFIT SURGED 201.8% YOY TO ₹74.1 CR, COMPARED WITH ₹24.6 CR LAST YEAR

• Q2 TOTAL INCOME UP 10% YOY TO ₹1,344 CR, WHILE EBITDA INCREASED 46.4% TO APPROXIMATELY ₹117.7 CR

• Q2 EBITDA MARGIN IMPROVED 220 BPS YOY TO 8.8%, WHILE NET PROFIT MARGIN EXPANDED 350 BPS TO 5.5%

• H1 EBITDA UP 24.9% YOY TO ₹225.7 CR, WHILE NET PROFIT INCREASED 78.3% TO ₹137.8 CR DESPITE LOWER REVENUE

INDO RAMA SYNTHETICS – Q2 CONCALL
#Q2FY27

Financial Performance
- Q2 net profit surged 201.8% YoY to ₹74.1 Cr.
- Q2 total income grew 10% YoY to ₹1,344 Cr.
- Q2 EBITDA increased 46.4% YoY to ₹117.7 Cr.
- EBITDA margin expanded 220 bps YoY to 8.8%.
- Net profit margin improved 350 bps YoY to 5.5%.
- H1 EBITDA rose 24.9% to ₹225.7 Cr; net profit grew 78.3% to ₹137.8 Cr.

FY27 Guidance & Margins
- Revenue target above ₹5,000 Cr and EBITDA above ₹400 Cr.
- Management expects EBITDA margins of around 9.9% to remain sustainable over the next two quarters.
- Long-term ambition is to achieve double-digit EBITDA margins.
- FY27 sales volume target is around 4 lakh tonnes versus 4.75 lakh tonnes in FY26.
- Volume recovery above FY26 levels targeted for FY28.

Specialty Expansion
- ₹200 Cr capex approved for specialty filament yarn and polyester fibre.
- Commercial operations targeted during calendar 2027.
- Project could add around 15% to revenue potential and 20% to EBITDA potential.
- Management estimates around ₹100 Cr annual EBITDA contribution around FY29.

Capacity & Exports
- Polyester fibre and filament operations are near full capacity.
- PET resin capacity utilisation stands at around 60%.
- Export contribution target is 20–25% of sales versus approximately 5.6% currently.

Cash Flow & Debt
- H1 operating cash flow improved to ₹328.5 Cr from around ₹92 Cr YoY.
- Net debt declined to ₹852 Cr from ₹1,113 Cr at FY26-end.

Key Risks
- Commodity price volatility and raw-material supply disruptions.
- Low PET resin utilisation.
- Debt-funded capex and execution of specialty expansion.

Key Takeaway
- Strong profit growth, improving cash flow and lower debt support the recovery.
- Specialty expansion offers incremental earnings potential from FY29.
- Achieving FY27 targets and sustaining margins remain key monitorables.

VEEFIN SOLUTIONS – Q2 CONCALL
#Q2FY27

Financial Performance
- H1 consolidated revenue grew 116.2% YoY to ₹238.82 Cr.
- H1 EBITDA rose 159.5% to ₹60.81 Cr; margin expanded 430 bps to 25.5%.
- Q2 revenue increased 9.2% QoQ to ₹124.66 Cr.
- Q2 EBITDA grew 52.2% QoQ to ₹36.70 Cr; margin improved to 29.4% from 21.1%.
- Q2 net profit rose 60.7% QoQ to ₹15.32 Cr.
- H1 standalone revenue grew 83.6% to ₹49.19 Cr; EBITDA increased 107.4% to ₹27.20 Cr.

Growth Outlook & Margins
- Management expects historical growth momentum to continue for around two years.
- No specific FY27 revenue guidance provided.
- Standalone EBITDA margin guidance remains at 45–50%.
- Management cautioned against extrapolating current margins above 55%.
- Product-development capitalization is expected to largely cease from FY28, increasing expenses recognised in the P&L.

Opportunity Pipeline
- Pipeline stands at approximately ₹920 Cr, including ₹240 Cr of new opportunities added in Q2.
- Around ₹46 Cr of opportunities were contracted during Q2.
- 75% of the open pipeline is fully qualified; pipeline is not a confirmed order book.
- International markets account for around 84% of the pipeline, led by Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa.
- Pipeline mix: Supply Chain Finance 35%, Digital Lending 23%, Trade & Cash Management 18%, Digital Banking 16%.

Business & Technology
- Existing customers contributed around 69.9% of quarterly revenue.
- Standalone recurring revenue reached 89.8%.
- Launched Veefin AI OS with 1,000+ reusable AI skills for banking automation, implementation, support and testing.

Key Risks & Monitorables
- Negative H1 operating cash flow; management expects recovery in H2.
- Unbilled revenue and development spending require monitoring.
- Pipeline conversion into contracted business remains critical.
- Higher P&L expenses from FY28 may affect reported margins.

Key Takeaway
- Strong H1 growth, margin expansion and a large international opportunity pipeline support business momentum.
- Cash-flow recovery, pipeline conversion and post-capitalisation profitability remain key monitorables.

Q2FY26 Concalls Highlights

NETWEB TECHNOLOGIES – Q2FY27 CONCALL
#Q2FY27

Financial Performance
- Q2 revenue rose 335.7% YoY to ₹1,323 Cr, up 61.4% QoQ.
- Operating EBITDA increased 334% YoY to ₹197 Cr; margin stood at 14.9%.
- Net profit surged approximately 335% YoY to ₹137 Cr.
- H1 revenue grew 254.2% to ₹2,143 Cr.
- H1 EBITDA rose 257.7% to ₹323 Cr; net profit increased 258.5% to ₹222 Cr.

AI Business & Growth
- AI Systems revenue surged 1,068% YoY to ₹773 Cr, contributing 58.4% of Q2 revenue.
- FY27 revenue target stands at ₹4,000 Cr; H1 has achieved ₹2,143 Cr.
- Management expects 30–40% annual revenue growth over the next 2–3 years.
- Medium-term EBITDA margin framework remains at 13–14%.

Order Book & Pipeline
- Confirmed order book stands at ₹2,629 Cr.
- L1 opportunities worth ₹653 Cr await final order conversion.
- Opportunity pipeline stands at ₹11,152 Cr, with historical conversion of around 60%.
- Pipeline is separate from the confirmed order book.

Key Risks
- High inventory levels and component cost inflation.
- Dependence on large customer orders.
- Execution risks in converting the opportunity pipeline into confirmed orders.

Key Takeaway
- AI Systems demand is driving exceptional revenue and earnings growth.
- FY27 target appears achievable based on H1 revenue, subject to execution in H2.
- Sustaining growth, managing working capital and maintaining margins remain key monitorables.

SUMITOMO CHEMICAL Q2: REVENUE DOWN 2% YOY; EBITDA MARGIN DECLINES 297 BPS, H2 OUTLOOK CHALLENGING

• Revenue: Down 2% YoY to ₹907 Cr in Q2 FY27; H1 revenue down 1% to ₹1,971 Cr

• Volume Pressure: Sales volumes declined by high-single-digit percentage amid weak agrochemical demand

• Domestic Business: Revenue up 2% YoY to ₹774 Cr, showing resilience despite challenging industry conditions

• Export Business: Revenue down 23% YoY to ₹127 Cr due to weak international demand

• Gross Margin: Declined 240 bps YoY to 40.7%, impacted by higher-cost inventory

• EBITDA Margin: Contracted 297 bps YoY to 20.5%, reflecting elevated raw material costs

• Inventory Costs: Higher-cost inventory purchased during Q1 impacted Q2 margins; mismatch largely normalised by quarter-end

• Industry Challenges: Delayed monsoon, 13% rainfall deficit and prolonged dry spells impacted crop sowing and agrochemical consumption

• Product Launches: Introduced Topgrain biostimulant and Helibex, strengthening the differentiated product portfolio

• Capacity Expansion: Ongoing capex progressing as planned, with production expected within previously announced timelines

• H2 FY27 Outlook: Management expects challenging demand conditions due to lower reservoir levels, extended El Niño impact and potential crop acreage constraints

• Growth Strategy: Focus on differentiated products, dynamic pricing, cost management and priority molecules to support performance

**ONE 97 COMMUNICATIONS (PAYTM) – GOLDMAN SACHS MAINTAINS BUY**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Goldman Sachs maintains **Buy** rating with a target price of ₹2,010.
- Q2FY27 revenue grew 28% YoY (33% like-for-like), with further acceleration expected as UPI MDR revenue starts flowing in.
- EBITDA beat Goldman Sachs estimates by 10%, with continued margin expansion.
- UPI MDR could improve payment processing margins by 2.5 bps, potentially contributing ₹800–900 Cr to FY28 EBITDA.
- Financial services growth accelerated, supported by improving personal loan trends.
- Meaningful revenue and EBITDA contribution from postpaid is expected from FY28.
- Payments market share improved for another quarter, with strong monthly transacting user (MTU) additions.
- Higher-than-expected device-related capex may increase depreciation and amortisation costs, leading to some EPS estimate cuts.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong revenue growth, margin expansion and potential UPI MDR benefits support the outlook.
- Higher capex and resulting depreciation costs remain key concerns.
- Impact: **Positive**

**ONE 97 COMMUNICATIONS (PAYTM) – CITI MAINTAINS BUY**

**Key Takeaway**
- Improving financial services growth and payment margins support the earnings outlook.
- Higher investments and DLG-related costs may weigh on near-term margins.
- Impact: **Positive**

TATA CONSUMER PRODUCTS - Q2FY27 RESULTS
#Q2FY27

FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
- Revenue ₹5,661 Cr vs estimate of ₹5,605 Cr
- EBITDA ₹783 Cr vs estimate of ₹775 Cr
- EBITDA margin 13.8%, in line with estimates
- PAT ₹470 Cr vs estimate of ₹456 Cr
- Revenue grew 14% YoY
- EBITDA grew 16.6% YoY
- PAT grew 15.7% YoY

INDIA BUSINESS
- Underlying volume growth stood at 11%
- Growth businesses recorded 40% growth
- Growth businesses contributed 38% of revenue vs 32% YoY
- Tata Sampann growth reached 57% vs expected 40-50%
- RTD business grew 47%, supported by a harsh summer
- Salt revenue grew 15%, with volume growth of 9%
- India Tea volumes remained flat; revenue declined 1% YoY

GROWTH BUSINESSES
- Capital Foods and Organic India combined sales reached ₹409 Cr vs expected ₹320-350 Cr
- Tata Starbucks revenue grew 15%, with multi-quarter high growth and strong SSSG

INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS
- International revenue grew 7%
- Constant-currency revenue declined 2%

MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY
- Maintains annual margin expansion target of 50-70 bps beyond commodity impacts
- Targets YoY margin expansion in H2FY27
- Maintains 30% growth guidance for growth businesses
- Targets mid-to-high single-digit growth in Tea and Salt

KEY TAKEAWAYS
- Revenue, EBITDA and PAT exceeded analyst estimates
- EBITDA margin remained in line with estimates at 13.8%
- Growth businesses continued to outperform, led by Tata Sampann, RTD, Capital Foods and Organic India
- Growth businesses increased their revenue contribution to 38%
- India Tea remained subdued, with flat volumes and lower revenue
- International growth was positive in reported terms but negative on a constant-currency basis
- Management retained its growth and margin expansion guidance

**MANKIND PHARMA – JPMORGAN MAINTAINS NEUTRAL**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- JPMorgan maintains **Neutral** rating with a target price of ₹2,700.
- Q2 revenue came 3% above estimates, driven by strong India Rx and healthy export growth, offsetting consumer business weakness.
- India business grew around 16% YoY, partly supported by a low base.
- EBITDA margin stood at 27%, around 100 bps above estimates.
- FY27 EBITDA margin guidance remains unchanged at 25.5–26.5%.
- Consumer business growth guidance cut to single digits from high-single-digit to double-digit growth.
- Management expects double-digit consumer growth from next year, supported by e-commerce and quick-commerce channels.
- E-commerce and quick-commerce mix rose to around 18% in Q2 from 12% last year.
- EBITDA estimates raised by 3–4% on better visibility in India Rx and exports.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong India Rx, exports and margin performance supported the Q2 beat.
- Sustainable India outperformance and consumer business recovery remain key monitorables.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**MANKIND PHARMA – BERNSTEIN MAINTAINS UNDERWEIGHT**
**Brokerage Update**

**Key Highlights**
- Bernstein maintains **Underweight (UW)** rating with a target price of ₹2,057.
- Q2FY27 results offered limited evidence to justify the company's premium valuation.
- Domestic business grew 15.9%, with gastro and vitamins improving, while anti-infectives grew 5.4% and consumer healthcare just 1.2%.
- Volume growth stood at 6.7%, supported by seasonal acute demand and an easier GST-affected base.
- New brand contribution remained limited, raising concerns about the sustainability of headline growth.
- Consumer recovery has been delayed again, highlighting concerns around weakening momentum and slow brand creation.
- Exports performed better than expected, while BSV continued to show improved execution.
- Margins beat estimates, but management retained its 25% margin guidance.

**Key Takeaway**
- Domestic growth and exports offer support, but recovery remains uneven.
- Consumer weakness, limited new-brand traction and premium valuation remain key concerns.
- Impact: **Negative**

INDIA APPROVES E100 FUEL FOR CERTIFIED FLEX-FUEL VEHICLES
Automobile & Ethanol Update

Key Highlights
- Centre amends Central Motor Vehicles Rules to recognise E100 fuel for OEM-certified flex-fuel vehicles.
- Conventional petrol cars and E20-only vehicles cannot use E100.
- E100 contains nearly pure ethanol, while E85 contains 85% ethanol.
- Maruti Suzuki has showcased its Wagon R flex-fuel prototype, compatible with E20 to E100.
- Initial flex-fuel outlets planned across Delhi-NCR and Mumbai-Pune-Nagpur corridors.
- Wider adoption depends on vehicle launches and fuel station availability.

Key Takeaway
- Policy supports ethanol adoption and India's efforts to reduce crude oil imports.
- Potential beneficiaries include ethanol producers, sugar companies and flex-fuel vehicle ecosystem players.
- Impact: Positive for ethanol ecosystem; gradual for automakers

Q2 FY27 Performance
- Revenue: ₹3,977 Cr, up 22% YoY.
- PBDIT: ₹319 Cr, down 22% YoY.
- PAT: ₹106 Cr vs ₹159 Cr YoY.
- Higher chemical input costs impacted profitability.

H1 FY27 Performance
- Revenue: ₹7,541 Cr, up 15% YoY.
- PBDIT: ₹683 Cr vs ₹734 Cr YoY.
- Reported PAT: ₹799 Cr vs ₹273 Cr YoY.
- PAT included ₹474.3 Cr tax adjustment and ₹79.4 Cr exceptional gains.
- Normalised PAT stood at ₹253 Cr.

Interim Dividend
- Board announced 200% interim dividend.
- Total dividend payout amounts to ₹62.38 Cr.

Segment Performance
- Chemicals: Revenue up 47% to ₹1,343 Cr.
- Vinyl: Revenue up 20% to ₹234 Cr.
- Sugar & Ethanol: Revenue up 10% to ₹1,023 Cr.
- Sugar & Ethanol PBDIT grew 85% to ₹62 Cr.
- Fenesta: Revenue up 22% to ₹344 Cr.
- Farm Solutions: Revenue fell to ₹423 Cr from ₹471 Cr.
- Fertilizer: Revenue up 40% to ₹502 Cr.
- Fertilizer PBDIT grew 25% to ₹25 Cr.
- Bioseed: Revenue fell to ₹73 Cr from ₹86 Cr.

Capacity Expansion & Outlook
- Commissioned Aluminium Chloride and partial Calcium Chloride plants.
- Fenesta commissioned Phase I Aluminium Extrusion Plant at Kota.
- Added 68 MW captive renewable energy capacity at Kota.
- New projects targeted by Q3 FY28.
- Focus remains on integration, cost control and efficiency.

Key Takeaway
- Revenue growth remains strong across several segments.
- Q2 profitability declined amid cost pressures and weaker agri earnings.
- H1 reported PAT benefited significantly from tax adjustment and exceptional gains.
- Impact: Mixed

- Industrial products delivered strong profit growth
- Packaging segment profit declined despite revenue growth

- EBITDA margin declined sequentially to 12.83%

**CLSA ON SBI CARDS – OUTPERFORM**
**Brokerage Update | Target Price: ₹700**

**Key Highlights**
- Q2FY27 PPoP was broadly in line with estimates.
- PAT beat estimates by 7%, driven by lower credit costs.
- Credit costs declined 100 bps QoQ to multi-quarter lows.
- Credit costs were 40 bps below expectations.
- Retail spend growth moderated to mid-single digits due to festive timing.
- Loan growth declined 2% YoY, similar to peers.
- Card acquisition momentum improved over the past two quarters.
- Calculated NIM remained largely stable at 11.8%.
- NIM may moderate slightly due to rate hikes.
- Fee income exceeded estimates, supported by higher interchange rates.

**Key Takeaway**
- Lower credit costs supported the PAT beat.
- Slower retail spending weighed on loan growth.
- Improved card acquisitions and fee income offer some support.
- Interest-rate increases may pressure future NIM.
- CLSA Rating: **Outperform**
- Target Price: **₹700**

**MACQUARIE ON SBI CARDS – NEUTRAL**
**Brokerage Update | Target Price: ₹600**

**Key Highlights**
- Q2FY27 earnings beat estimates, but underlying growth remains subdued.
- Margin protection is expected to remain challenging.
- Asset quality showed improvement.
- Stage 2 provision coverage increased 60 bps QoQ.
- Company added a ₹30 Cr overlay.
- Total overlay provisions increased to ₹100 Cr.

**Management Guidance**
- Credit costs expected to remain at 5.5–6.0% going forward.

**Key Takeaway**
- Earnings exceeded estimates, but growth momentum remains weak.
- Improving asset quality supports the outlook.
- Margin pressure and elevated credit costs remain key concerns.
- Macquarie Rating: **Neutral**
- Target Price: **₹600**

**UBS ON SBI CARDS – NEUTRAL**
**Brokerage Update | Target Price: ₹635**

**Key Highlights**
- Q2FY27 PAT grew 75% YoY to ₹780 Cr.
- PAT exceeded UBS estimates by 9%, driven by lower credit costs.
- Receivables grew just 0.2% QoQ and declined 2.5% YoY.
- NII remained flat YoY, reflecting weak receivables growth.
- PPoP declined 1.4% YoY, in line with estimates.
- Credit costs stood at ₹820 Cr, or 5.6% of average receivables.
- Credit costs declined 37% YoY and were 7% below UBS estimates.
- Retail spends grew 6% YoY.
- Fee and commission income increased 7.4% YoY.

**Management Outlook**
- Management expects spends and receivables to improve from Q3FY27.
- Further credit-cost improvement appears limited from current levels.

**Key Monitorables**
- Conversion of retail spends into interest-earning receivables.
- Ability to sustain margins amid rising funding costs.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong PAT growth was primarily driven by lower credit costs.
- Weak receivables growth continues to constrain NII.
- Future earnings growth depends on improving spends and receivables.
- UBS Rating: **Neutral**
- Target Price: **₹635**

**BERNSTEIN ON SBI CARDS – UNDERPERFORM**
**Brokerage Update | Target Price: ₹430**

**Key Highlights**
- Q2FY27 PAT grew 75% YoY, indicating a sharp earnings recovery.
- Lower credit costs were the primary driver of profit growth.
- Retail spends growth moderated to 6%.
- Stable revolver share offers some support.
- However, structural pressure on interest-earning balances remains unresolved.
- Credit costs are approaching steady-state levels.
- Further earnings growth may be limited without a meaningful recovery in spends.
- Recovery in interest-earning advances is also critical.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong PAT growth was largely credit-cost driven.
- Underlying spending growth remains weak.
- Stable revolver share has yet to reverse pressure on interest-earning balances.
- Earnings growth depends on recovery in spends and advances.
- Bernstein Rating: **Underperform**
- Target Price: **₹430**

**CITI ON JSW STEEL – SELL**
**Brokerage Update | Target Price: ₹1,135**

**Key Highlights**
- Q2FY27 consolidated EBITDA stood at ₹9,940 Cr, 3% above estimates.
- EBITDA grew 39% YoY, driven by higher volumes and realizations.
- India volumes increased 14% YoY.
- Realizations rose 14% YoY, partly offset by 12% higher costs.
- India EBITDA per tonne stood at ₹13,250.
- EBITDA per tonne declined from ₹15,110 in Q1FY27.
- Net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.3x from 1.5x in June 2026.
- Q2 capacity utilisation stood at approximately 88%.
- Q2 realizations declined less than 1% QoQ.
- Q3 realizations are expected to offset higher costs.
- Coking coal costs rose $10/tonne in Q2.
- Another $25/tonne increase is expected in Q3FY27.

**Expansion & Capex**
- Odisha Phase II project involves 5 MT capacity expansion.
- JSW JFE expansion involves another 5 MT.
- JSW Steel capacity targeted to rise from 32 MT to 54 MT+.
- JSW JFE capacity targeted to increase from 4.5 MT to 9.5 MT by FY31.
- Planned capex after H1FY27 stands at approximately ₹1,48,400 Cr.
- Citi estimates JSW JFE expansion capex at ₹30,000 Cr.
- JSW JFE quarterly EBITDA is estimated at ₹1,100 Cr, with net debt of approximately ₹21,500 Cr.

**Key Concerns**
- Citi sees potential downside to spot India EBITDA per tonne.
- Flat steel prices remain ₹2,500/tonne above import parity.
- China demand remains weak, down approximately 3% YTD.
- Funding for the JSW JFE expansion remains uncertain.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong Q2 EBITDA growth was supported by volumes and realizations.
- Rising coking coal costs may pressure Q3 profitability.
- Large expansion plans raise capex and funding concerns.
- Citi Rating: **Sell**
- Target Price: **₹1,135**

**JEFFERIES ON JSW STEEL – BUY**
**Brokerage Update | Target Price: ₹1,650**

**Key Highlights**
- Q2FY27 EBITDA grew 8% QoQ, in line with Jefferies estimates.
- India steel prices have risen 15% since August 2026.
- Higher steel prices are expected to offset rising input costs.
- Margins are expected to expand.
- Announced 10 MT capacity expansions strengthen the growth outlook.
- Expansion plans support the target to double capacity by FY32.
- Stock trades at 8x one-year forward EV/EBITDA.
- Jefferies considers current valuation justified.

**Earnings Outlook**
- FY27–FY29E EPS estimates raised by 2–4%.
- EPS is expected to treble over FY26–FY29.

**Key Takeaway**
- Higher steel prices could drive margin expansion.
- Capacity expansion strengthens long-term growth visibility.
- Earnings upgrades support the positive outlook.
- Jefferies Rating: **Buy**
- Target Price: **₹1,650**

**CLSA ON JSW STEEL – OUTPERFORM**
**Brokerage Update | Target Price: ₹1,500**

**Key Highlights**
- Q2FY27 EBITDA slightly exceeded estimates.
- Higher volumes and stronger subsidiary profitability supported performance.
- Q3 profitability is expected to improve.
- Higher steel prices and softer iron ore costs should support margins.
- Operating leverage is expected to offset coking coal cost pressures.

**Growth Outlook**
- Capacity expansion approvals at JSW Utkal and JJSL improve long-term growth visibility.
- Expansion plans reinforce the pathway towards 80 MT capacity.

**Key Takeaway**
- Q2 EBITDA beat estimates on stronger volumes and subsidiaries.
- Steel price improvement and lower iron ore costs may support Q3 margins.
- Capacity expansion strengthens the long-term growth outlook.
- CLSA Rating: **Outperform**
- Target Price: **₹1,500**

**CITI ON JSPL – SELL**
**Brokerage Update | Target Price Cut to ₹850 from ₹900**

**Key Highlights**
- Q2FY27 consolidated adjusted EBITDA stood at ₹2,500 Cr.
- EBITDA grew 34% YoY, supported by higher volumes and realizations.
- Sales volumes increased 27% YoY.
- Blended realizations improved 12% YoY.
- Higher costs, up 14%, partly offset the gains.
- Adjusted EBITDA per tonne stood at ₹10,520.
- EBITDA per tonne declined from ₹11,960 in Q1FY27.
- EBITDA per tonne improved from ₹10,030 last year.
- Blended realizations increased ₹650/tonne QoQ.
- Further coking coal cost increases are expected in Q3FY27.

**Management Guidance**
- FY27 sales target retained at 10.5–11 MT.
- Target implies 21–26% YoY growth.
- H1FY27 sales grew 22% to 4.61 MT.
- JSPL plans to increase flat steel contribution from 61% to 65%.

**Key Concerns**
- Higher spot prices may offer limited incremental benefits.
- Citi sees potential downside to spot India EBITDA per tonne.
- Flat steel prices remain at a ₹2,500/tonne premium to import parity.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong volume growth and realizations supported Q2 EBITDA growth.
- Rising input costs remain a margin headwind.
- Potential steel price weakness and limited spot-price upside weigh on the outlook.
- Citi Rating: **Sell**
- Target Price: **Cut to ₹850 from ₹900**

- Q2FY27 reported a marginal headline miss, but underlying performance remained strong.
- Cost synergies of ₹450 Cr from the JB Pharma acquisition are now expected within two years.
- Earlier guidance indicated a three-year timeline for synergy realisation.
- Torrent expects EBITDA margins to improve marginally in H2FY27 versus H1FY27.
- Margin improvement depends on stabilisation of JB Pharma operations.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong core performance contrasts with the marginal headline miss.
- Faster synergy realisation could support profitability.

- JB Pharma integration is progressing ahead of schedule.

**Growth Catalysts**
- Revenue synergies are expected to drive strong India growth next year.
- Continued India and Brazil momentum supports the growth outlook.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong base business growth continues across key markets.
- Faster synergy realisation supports the integration outlook.
- Revenue synergies could accelerate India growth next year.
- Jefferies Rating: **Buy**
- Target Price: **₹5,900**

**CITI ON TORRENT PHARMA – BUY**
**Brokerage Update | Target Price: ₹5,860**

**Key Highlights**
- Q2FY27 performance was in line with expectations.
- Base business delivered robust growth, led by India and Brazil.
- JB Pharma faced temporary post-merger integration challenges.
- Postponed deliveries in select international markets also impacted JB Pharma.
- Management expects JB Pharma's recovery to be gradual.
- H2 India growth expected to exceed the approximately 10% achieved in H1.

- Consolidated margins are expected to improve from 33.5% in Q2FY27.

- Strong base business growth continues to support performance.
- JB Pharma recovery remains gradual but is expected to improve in H2.
- Faster synergy realisation could support margin expansion.

- JB Pharma sales were impacted by post-merger integration activities.
- HSBC sees scope for EBITDA margin expansion.
- Sustained branded generics growth, particularly in India, could drive margins.

**Key Catalyst**
- Recovery in JB Pharma portfolio growth remains the next key catalyst.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong India base business growth supports the outlook.
- Margin expansion depends on sustained branded generics growth.
- JB Pharma's post-merger growth recovery remains crucial.

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
